name.en: NACO Canada — National Angel Capital Organization

strategy.thesis: National umbrella / industry association for angel investors and angel groups across Canada; provides directory, education, advocacy and the Co-Investment Summit. Not itself a deal-investing group but the apex body for the segment.

summary.en: NACO Canada, founded in 2002, is the national industry association for angel investors in Canada. Its network spans roughly 4,200 angel investors, 44 angel groups and 45 incubators/accelerators, and member activity exceeds C$1.9 billion deployed since 2010.

sources.title: NACO Canada — National Angel Capital Organization
sources.supports: capital deployed, companies funded, investor base

sources.quote: Its national network now includes 4,200 angel investors, 45 incubators and accelerators, and 44 angel groups.

verification_notes: Founding year (2002) and founder (Henry Vehovec) corroborated by Wikipedia and multiple secondary sources. NACO is the apex association rather than a deal-doing angel group; included for segment completeness.

strategy.thesis: Largest angel investor network in Canada; members invest capital and expertise into innovative pre-seed/seed Quebec companies and actively mentor founders. A co-investment fund, AQC Capital, runs alongside the network.

summary.en: Anges Québec, founded in 2008, is described as the largest angel investor network in Canada, with 230+ members who have invested more than C$171M in nearly 200 innovative Quebec companies.
summary.local: Anges Québec, fondé en 2008, est le plus grand réseau d'anges investisseurs au Canada, comptant plus de 230 membres ayant investi plus de 171 M$ dans près de 200 entreprises innovantes du Québec.

strategy.thesis: One of Canada's oldest and largest angel networks; supports BC-based technology founders with angel capital, advice and connections via monthly pitch presentations.

summary.en: VANTEC, founded in Vancouver in 1999, is one of Canada's oldest and largest angel networks. It has 200+ members and has presented more than 2,500 entrepreneurs to angel investors, supporting BC-based technology founders.

strategy.thesis: Not-for-profit membership organization connecting accredited investors with seed and early-stage Canadian startups; describes itself as Toronto's largest angel network.

summary.en: Maple Leaf Angels, established in 2007 and based in Toronto, is a not-for-profit angel membership organization whose members have invested over C$44 million in 102 seed and early-stage companies.

strategy.thesis: Canadian arm of the global invitation-only Keiretsu Forum angel network; sector-agnostic, funds life sciences, medtech, cleantech, fintech, technology, consumer and travel companies across four Ontario chapters.

summary.en: Keiretsu Forum Canada, established in 2012, is the Canadian arm of the world's largest invitation-only angel investor network. It operates four Ontario chapters (London, Waterloo, York Region, Toronto); Canadian members allocated $16.8M to early-stage companies in 2021.

strategy.thesis: Ottawa-Gatineau regional angel network of 55+ investors (including VCs and family offices); invests across software, hardware, cleantech, agtech, biotech and SaaS, with ~90% of portfolio in the Ottawa region.

summary.en: Capital Angel Network, founded in 2009 in Ottawa, has 55+ investor members (30% women) and has backed 180 companies, with $77M of overall investments since 2010 and $41M into early-stage Canadian startups since 2021.

strategy.thesis: Waterloo Region angel network of angels, super angels, family offices and venture funds; one of Canada's most active early-stage investors and a founding member of Equation Angels.

summary.en: Golden Triangle Angel Network (GTAN), founded in 2008 in Waterloo, has members who have invested over C$60M of angel capital into more than 150 companies, catalyzing over a billion dollars in follow-on capital.

strategy.thesis: Not-for-profit network of high-net-worth investors across Toronto, Mississauga, Oakville, Burlington and Hamilton; a founding partner of Equation Angels.

summary.en: Angel One Investor Network, formed in September 2011 and based in Burlington, has made over 137 investments in 81 startup and growth-stage companies, with more than C$29.2 million invested. It is a founding partner of Equation Angels.

strategy.thesis: Non-profit group of accredited investors in York Region (Markham, Richmond Hill, Vaughan, Aurora, Newmarket); invests in IT, internet, enterprise/SaaS, retail and pharma startups.

summary.en: York Angel Investors, founded in 2008 in Markham by Scott MacCannell, is a non-profit network of accredited investors. From 2008 to 2019 it invested in over 40 deals totaling roughly C$10.8M, with two exits.

strategy.thesis: The only accredited angel organization in Northern Ontario; a not-for-profit catalyst connecting entrepreneurs and investors across Sudbury, Thunder Bay, Sault Ste. Marie, North Bay, Timmins and Kenora.

summary.en: Northern Ontario Angels, established in 2005 and based in Thunder Bay, is the only accredited angel organization in Northern Ontario. It reports investing over C$780M into 500+ firms, including Flosonics Medical and iRegained.

strategy.thesis: Members-only non-profit of accredited investors in the London/Southwestern Ontario region; a founding member of Equation Angels.

summary.en: The Southwestern Ontario Angel Group (SWO Angels), founded in 2008 in London, Ontario, is a members-only non-profit of accredited investors that has invested over C$21.5 million in 70 investments and is a founding member of Equation Angels.

strategy.thesis: Collaboration of Southern Ontario angel groups (GTAN, Angel One, SWO Angels, WECAN) pooling deal flow and ~200 angels; described as one of Canada's largest angel networks.

summary.en: Equation Angels, launched in October 2019, is a collaboration of Southern Ontario angel groups (Angel One, GTAN, SWO Angels and the Windsor Essex Capital Angel Network) bringing together nearly 200 angel investors — described as the second-largest angel network in Canada.

strategy.thesis: Runs angel syndicates and Investment Summits across Western Canada that onboard new and seasoned angels; all deals are syndicated through an LP for a single cap-table line, with a co-invest VC fund (TNT Capital) backing each summit winner.

summary.en: Startup TNT, founded in 2019 and based in Edmonton, runs angel syndicates and Investment Summits across Western Canada. Over five years it has hosted 30 summits, engaged 375 angel investors and facilitated C$12.5M into 90 startups; angels can invest as little as $5,000 and its TNT Capital fund co-invests $50,000 per summit winner.

strategy.thesis: Described as the largest angel network in Western Canada; runs private investor forums in Edmonton, Calgary, Kelowna and Vancouver, now part of full-service corporate-finance firm Valhalla Private Capital.

summary.en: Valhalla Angels began in 2003 as a single-city angel group and grew into what it describes as the largest angel network in Western Canada, holding private investor forums in Edmonton, Calgary, Kelowna and Vancouver under Valhalla Private Capital.

strategy.thesis: Cross-city network of all-women angel funds; partners commit capital, meet monthly, build a shared thesis and back women-run/women-led businesses (70%+ of investments). Billed as Canada's first all-female angel fund.

summary.en: Women's Equity Lab, launched in Victoria, BC in late 2017 by 23 founding partners with NACO support, is Canada's first all-female angel fund. It now has 400+ women investors across BC, the Prairies, Ontario, Atlantic Canada and Silicon Valley, investing in 50+ companies (70%+ women-led); investors commit $5,500 per fund.

strategy.thesis: Network of women angels investing in women-led technology startups, centred on the Toronto-Waterloo corridor with national coverage; manages a committed-capital fund model.

summary.en: The Firehood, founded in 2021, is a network of 100+ women angels backing women in tech. It has invested over C$2M in 10 startups from Vancouver to Newfoundland, centred on the Toronto-Waterloo corridor.

strategy.thesis: Financial platform, venture firm and investment collective directing capital to women-led ventures; runs an angel/investor community alongside managed funds (Fund III), networking and education.

summary.en: The51, launched in Calgary in 2019, is a financial platform, venture firm and investment collective focused on women-led companies. It reports $71M+ capital activated across 200+ ventures (81% led by women CEOs), combining managed funds with an angel/investor community.

strategy.thesis: Member-based not-for-profit that bridged the capital gap for Atlantic Canadian companies; was the region's most active angel network before winding down.

summary.en: First Angel Network, founded in 2005 in Halifax, was Atlantic Canada's most active angel network until it wound down on March 31, 2019. Its 200+ members invested roughly C$16M in 40 Atlantic Canadian companies including Proposify and LeadSift.

sources.title: Atlantic Canada's First Angel Network shuts down

sources.quote: the First Angel Network is concluding its work ... over 200 angel investor members to invest in 40 Atlantic Canada companies, representing $16 million in total capital commitment since its founding

verification_notes: Wound down effective 2019-03-31; status set to inactive. Included for segment completeness as a historically significant Atlantic angel network.
